validation.valueRange: Enter a value between 1.1–33.3 mmol/L (20–600 mg/dL).
validation.dateInvalid: Please choose a valid date and time.
validation.dateFuture: The time can't be in the future.
validation.duplicate: A reading with the same value and time already exists.
validation.describe: Please describe what you'd like to log.

glucose.moreDetails: Add symptoms, meal, activity or medication (optional)
glucose.saved: Reading saved. Your history, chart and reports are updated.
glucose.savedLow: Reading saved. This is below the demo low threshold — if you feel shaky, sweaty or confused, follow your clinic's low-glucose advice or call 999.
glucose.savedVeryHigh: Reading saved. This is very high — if you feel very unwell, vomiting or drowsy, seek urgent care (999).

chart.empty: No readings in this period yet.
chart.aria: Glucose chart with {{n}} recorded readings in mmol/L
chart.band: Demo reference range {{lo}}–{{hi}} mmol/L (not a personal target)

urgent.title: Possible urgent situation
urgent.body: If you feel very unwell, confused, faint, have chest pain or trouble breathing, call 999 or go to the nearest emergency department now. Don't wait for a caregiver to respond.

overview.summaryOk: No repeated out-of-range pattern in your recent records.
overview.summaryWatch: Some recent readings are worth reviewing — see your insight below.
overview.summarySafety: A reading needs attention — please read the guidance below.
overview.stale: Your last reading was {{when}}. Consider recording a new one.
overview.morningInsight: Your morning glucose readings were above the configured reference range ({{high}} mmol/L) on {{above}} of the last {{total}} recorded mornings.
overview.notEnoughMornings: Not enough morning readings yet for an insight.
overview.morningRule: Rule: last {{n}} recorded fasting readings compared with the demo reference {{high}} mmol/L.
limitationList: Uses demo thresholds, not your personal targets.
Shows what was recorded, not why it changed.
Days without readings are not counted.
overview.stepOk: Keep logging at your agreed times so patterns can be checked.
overview.stepWatch: Keep recording your morning readings, and add this to your questions for your next visit.
overview.stepSafety: Contact your clinic about this reading. If you feel unwell, seek urgent care (999).
overview.disclaimer: Insights come from simple, transparent rules applied to your records using demo thresholds. They show what changed — not why — and are not a diagnosis.

safety-low.title: Low readings recorded: {{n}}
safety-low.summary: A reading below {{hypo}} mmol/L was recorded in the last 7 days.
safety-low.rule: Any reading below {{hypo}} mmol/L in the last 7 days.
safety-low.next: Follow your clinic's low-glucose advice. If unwell, call 999.

safety-high.title: Very high readings recorded: {{n}}
safety-high.summary: A reading above {{high}} mmol/L was recorded in the last 7 days.
safety-high.rule: Any reading above {{high}} mmol/L in the last 7 days.
safety-high.next: If you feel very unwell, seek urgent care (999). Contact your clinic.

repeated-fasting.title: Morning readings above range on several days
repeated-fasting.summary: {{n}} of {{total}} fasting readings in the last 7 days were above {{high}} mmol/L.
repeated-fasting.rule: At least {{min}} fasting readings above {{high}} mmol/L within 7 days.
repeated-fasting.next: Keep recording and discuss at your next visit.

repeated-postmeal.title: Evening / after-meal readings above range
repeated-postmeal.summary: {{n}} after-meal or bedtime readings in the last 7 days were above {{high}} mmol/L.
repeated-postmeal.rule: At least {{min}} after-meal readings above {{high}} mmol/L within 7 days.
repeated-postmeal.next: Note meals around these readings and discuss with your doctor.

baseline-shift.title: Fasting average higher than your usual
baseline-shift.summary: Recent fasting average {{recent}} mmol/L vs earlier {{base}} mmol/L (+{{diff}}).
baseline-shift.rule: 7-day fasting average at least {{shift}} mmol/L above the previous 3 weeks (needs ≥{{min}} earlier readings).
baseline-shift.next: Add this to your questions for the doctor.

baseline-insufficient.title: Not enough data for a personal baseline yet
baseline-insufficient.summary: Found {{nb}} earlier and {{nr}} recent fasting readings.
baseline-insufficient.rule: Needs at least {{min}} earlier and 3 recent fasting readings.
baseline-insufficient.sufficiency: We can't compare with your usual levels yet.

insufficient-data.title: Few readings this week
insufficient-data.summary: Only {{n}} reading(s) in the last 7 days.
insufficient-data.rule: Needs at least 3 readings in 7 days.
insufficient-data.next: Record readings at your agreed times.

data-gap.title: Days without readings: {{n}}
data-gap.summary: No readings were recorded on these days. This is not treated as a health change.
data-gap.rule: Checks each of the last 7 full days for at least one reading.
data-gap.next: Try to record at least once a day.

unusual-entry.title: Unusual entries to check
unusual-entry.summary: Some readings changed by more than 8 mmol/L within an hour — possibly an entry or unit error.
unusual-entry.rule: Consecutive readings within 1 hour differing by more than 8 mmol/L.

health.subtitle: Record readings and see how they change over time.
health.baselineInsufficient: Not enough readings yet to calculate your usual level.
health.medNoteHint: Medication notes are your own records. A day without a log doesn't mean a dose was missed.
health.patternsIntro: Each observation uses a fixed, reviewable rule on your records with demo thresholds. Not a diagnosis.

med.inAppOnly: In-app reminders work while the app is open. Nothing is sent when the browser is closed.

med.prescribedOnly: Enter only what your doctor prescribed. This app never prescribes or changes doses.
med.name: Medication name

err.name: Please enter the medication name.

care.subtitle: Doctor-agreed goals, daily guide, medication and progress.
care.goalsNotice: Goals are set by your doctor. AI suggestions never change them. These demo goals are simulated.

ci.goal: Did you follow your agreed goal?
ci.autoGlucose: A reading was found for today.

meals.generalNotice: General education only — not a clinically personalised meal plan. Ask a dietitian for advice for you.
meals.prefNotice: Filtered by preferences you entered. Still general education, not a clinical meal plan.
meals.allergyNote: You noted allergies ({{a}}). Always check ingredients.
meals.prefsHint: We only use what you tell us. We never guess medical diet restrictions.

balanced.title: Balanced meals (suku-suku separuh)
balanced.body: Half the plate vegetables, a quarter protein (fish, chicken, tofu, eggs), a quarter carbohydrates (rice, noodles, bread).

carbs.title: Carbohydrate choices
carbs.body: Wholegrain options like brown rice, wholemeal bread, oats and chapati are often discussed as better choices than refined white rice or white bread.

portion.title: Portion awareness
portion.body: Try a smaller rice portion, ask for 'nasi separuh', and fill up on vegetables.

drinks.title: Sugary drinks
drinks.body: Choose plain water, 'kosong' or 'kurang manis' drinks instead of teh tarik, sirap or soft drinks.

timing.title: Meal timing
timing.body: Regular meal times can help, especially if you take diabetes medication. Ask your doctor about late dinners.

labels.title: Nutrition labels
labels.body: Check 'Jumlah Gula / Total sugar' and carbohydrate per serving on packaged foods. Look for the Healthier Choice logo.

wholemealEgg.name: Wholemeal bread & boiled egg
wholemealEgg.desc: With unsweetened tea or kopi-o kosong and a small fruit portion.

oatsNuts.name: Oats with nuts
oatsNuts.desc: Plain oats with a few nuts, no added sugar.

thosaiDhal.name: Thosai with dhal
thosaiDhal.desc: One thosai with dhal, plain drink.

nasiLemakSmall.name: Nasi lemak (small portion)
nasiLemakSmall.desc: Half rice, egg, cucumber, little sambal; skip fried sides.

chickenPorridge.name: Chicken porridge
chickenPorridge.desc: Small bowl with lean chicken and vegetables.

brownRiceFish.name: Brown rice, grilled fish & vegetables
brownRiceFish.desc: A balanced plate following the suku-suku separuh idea.

nasiCampur.name: Nasi campur (smart choice)
nasiCampur.desc: Half rice, two vegetable dishes and one non-fried protein.

yongTauFoo.name: Yong tau foo (soup)
yongTauFoo.desc: Choose vegetables and tofu, clear soup, fewer fried items.

chapatiDhal.name: Chapati with dhal & vegetables
chapatiDhal.desc: Wholemeal chapati with dhal and sabzi.

steamedChicken.name: Steamed chicken with vegetables
steamedChicken.desc: Skinless steamed chicken, small rice, greens.

vegSoupTofu.name: Clear vegetable soup with tofu
vegSoupTofu.desc: With a small portion of rice or noodles.

ikanBakar.name: Ikan bakar with ulam
ikanBakar.desc: Grilled fish, ulam and a small portion of rice.

clearSoupChicken.name: Clear chicken soup
clearSoupChicken.desc: With vegetables and a small portion of rice.

nuts.name: A small handful of unsalted nuts

activity.title: Activity guide

walk.name: Gentle walking
walk.desc: 10–30 minutes at a comfortable pace, e.g. after dinner.

stretch.name: Light stretching
stretch.desc: Slow stretches for arms, legs and back.

lowImpact.name: Low-impact activity
lowImpact.desc: Cycling slowly, swimming or tai chi.

chair.name: Chair-based exercise
chair.desc: Seated leg lifts and arm movements, good for limited mobility.

cautions: These are not safe for everyone — ask your doctor first.
If you take insulin or sulphonylureas, you may be at risk of low glucose; carry a sugary snack.
Stop if you feel dizzy, shaky, short of breath or have chest pain.
Wear comfortable shoes and check your feet.

copilot.subtitle: Diabetes education and help understanding your records.
copilot.demoTitle: Demo assistant — no AI or medical-source service is connected yet.
copilot.demoBody: Answers are pre-written demo responses using your records. It can't diagnose, prescribe or change medication. For chest pain, fainting, confusion or other urgent symptoms, call 999.
copilot.shareRecords: Allow the Copilot to use my recorded data
suggestions: Can you explain my recent glucose trend?
What should I ask my doctor?
What are some diabetes-friendly Malaysian meals?
copilot.noSources: No sources were retrieved — the medical-reference service isn't connected in this demo. Please confirm with your healthcare team.

r.urgent: These symptoms may need urgent attention. Please don't rely on this app. Call 999 or go to the nearest emergency department, or contact your clinic immediately.
r.noPrescribe: I can't recommend starting, stopping or changing medication or doses. Please discuss this with your doctor or pharmacist.
r.trendIntro: Here's what your recorded data shows (rule-based monitoring, not a diagnosis):
r.noPattern: No repeated out-of-range pattern in the last 7 days.
r.morning: Your morning readings were above {{high}} mmol/L on {{above}} of the last {{total}} recorded mornings.
r.noBaseline: There isn't enough earlier data to compare with your usual levels.
r.trendOutro: Late dinners and late nights were also logged on some days. These happened around the same time; the records don't prove one caused the other. Your doctor can help interpret this.
r.medIntro: Your prescribed schedule for today (from your own records):
r.medOutro: I can't change your medication. Ask your doctor about any concerns.
r.doctorIntro: Based on your records, you might ask:
doctorQs: My morning readings have been higher — what could be contributing?
Are my target ranges right for me?
Should I change my dinner or sleep times?
When should I contact the clinic between visits?
r.doctorOutro: You'll find these on the Doctor Visit report too.
r.goalOutro: Complete your daily check-in on My Care Plan.
r.mealIntro: General ideas often discussed in diabetes education (not personalised):
mealTips: Use the 'suku-suku separuh' plate: half vegetables, a quarter protein, a quarter carbs.
Choose brown rice or a smaller rice portion.
Ikan bakar, clear soups and tofu are lighter than deep-fried dishes.
Ask for 'kurang manis' or plain drinks.
r.mealOutro: A dietitian can tailor this to you.
r.terms: HbA1c reflects average glucose over about 2–3 months. Fasting glucose is measured before eating in the morning. Your doctor decides your personal targets.
r.fallback: I'm a demo assistant. I can explain your recent glucose trend, list today's medication schedule, prepare doctor questions and share general Malaysian meal ideas.
